validity: Thresholds are conventions chosen for reproducibility, calibrated to nothing yet (there is no benchmark corpus): a score is a pure function of the counters, not a measurement of quality.

styling.label: styling code is present in the audited folders
styling.note: no styling code in the audited folders: no markup or style files and no styling counter above 0

tailwind.label: a Tailwind class vocabulary is present
tailwind.note: no Tailwind class vocabulary found (no font-size, spacing or radius utilities, no default-palette classes, no @theme rule): the items that read Tailwind classes are not rated

markup.label: component source files are present
markup.note: no markup files (tsx, jsx, vue, svelte) among the audited files: the item is not rated

components_dir.label: a components/ folder is present
components_dir.note: no component files under a components/ folder: the item is not rated

instruction_body.label: the root instruction files hold at least 10 lines
instruction_body.note: the root instruction files hold fewer than 10 lines in all: an empty or stub file is not credited

instruction_headings.label: the root instruction files hold at least 2 headings
instruction_headings.note: the root instruction files hold fewer than 2 headings: lines without structure are not credited

limits: The overall is a rubric score over documentation and code signals, not a readiness measurement: documentation items count structure and length, so filler files can earn them. The docs_need_code cap bounds that only when the code ignores the documents.

27 of 60 points read names or files that only a Systemix-style repo has (design/guardrails.mdx, design/DESIGN.md, design/tokens.css, decisions/ and design/decisions/, contract/tokens records, .systemix/drift-history.json, scripts/*drift*, a workflow that mentions drift, slash-named skills): a repo with other conventions loses them whatever its practice, and Captured rationale and Codified rules read nothing else.
Every share divides by all audited files; adding files with no styling raises it.

overall.label: rubric score (not a measurement of readiness)

underserved: only dimensions with satisfaction below importance are ranked; the others are listed as satisfied

ratio.zero_note: the scanner audited no files: drift control not rated

unless.note: fewer than 60 percent of the audited files are free of raw colour literals, or the scanner audited none

caps.text: documents are credited above 6 of 10 only when the code follows them: styling code is present and at least 60 percent of the audited files hold no raw colour literal

inputs.relation: same counters for spacing, type, radius; colour literals belong to drift_control; not a score input
not an input: it reads raw px values, which belong to token_discipline
not an input: health is a separate line, so that nothing is counted twice (drift control and components enter through their own items)

dimensions.label: Captured rationale
dimensions.limit: Documentation items count structure and length, not truth: a file of filler can earn them, which is why the docs_need_code cap exists. Every item reads a Systemix-style path: decisions/ and design/decisions/ (the ADR items), design/DESIGN.md or a root DESIGN.md (the DESIGN.md items), contract/tokens records (the two token-record items); a repo that keeps its rationale elsewhere scores 0 here whatever its practice.

dimensions.label: Token discipline
dimensions.limit: A missing token source zeroes token_source and both wiring items together (3 of 10 points), because wiring is measured against the source; renormalising instead would raise the score when the token file is deleted. A named size such as text-sm counts as on-token only when the theme maps that very name, in both this dimension and design-audit tokens.type. Font-size, spacing, palette and radius items read Tailwind class spellings and are not rated without a Tailwind vocabulary; a token reached only through var() outside the --font-size-*, --text-* and --space-* families is invisible here. When a measure has nothing to count (no font-size utilities, no radius utilities) it earns full points, but only where styling code exists. type_scale_wired and spacing_scale_wired subtract the number of names the theme maps from the number of tokens with no var() consumer without intersecting the two lists (the language has no set operator): a mapped token that is also consumed hides a token that is really unwired, so the two items can over-award.

dimensions.label: Component consistency
dimensions.limit: A canonical tag renders the components/ui definition, a package, or the only definition of its name in the project; Button, Badge, Card and Input are the only primitives. The ratio weighs every tag the same and needs 5 tags before it is rated. Live reuse (canonical users that no file imports) is a report line, not an item: it overlaps dead_components. dead_components is not rated (0 points) when no component file outside components/ui is seen, because a layout that keeps components elsewhere (src/features/) is invisible to the counter.

items.label: Tag-weighted canonical reuse over Button, Badge, Card, Input (same measure as design-audit sub-score components)

ratio.min_den_note: fewer than 5 Button, Badge, Card or Input tags outside components/ui/: too few to rate, components not rated
ratio.zero_note: no Button, Badge, Card or Input usage found: components not rated

ratio.zero_note: no component files outside components/ui/ were seen: dead components not rated (components kept in another layout, such as src/features/, are invisible to this counter)

dimensions.limit: The instruction items count length, headings and pointers, not whether the instructions are right. guardrails_pointer is worth 0.5 because the counter only sees a mention of the word, not an instruction to read the guardrails before UI work.
